messages:
ana (sales): Hey team — kicking off NovusHealth private POC. They want a node validation checklist and a quick smoke-run on one of their jumpbox nodes before we book an install window. Main asks: GPU driver, CUDA runtime, container runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit / containerd), kubernetes compatibility, and kernel module status. Also they asked how Hosted API keys map to Private — want to confirm auth model (service account tokens + mTLS).
meera (eng-infra): Got it. Can you give me the jumpbox IP and a single node IP? We'll run a quick script. Also need distro + kernel.
nana (sales): jumpbox 10.20.5.12 (bastion), node to test 10.20.5.18. Node is Ubuntu 22.04, stock 5.15 kernel.
sam (field-eng): leaving short checklist here for the run:
- check GPU visible: `nvidia-smi`
- check driver module: `sudo modinfo nvidia` and `lsmod | grep nvidia`
- check cuda toolkit: `nvcc --version` or `cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt`
- container runtime: `containerd --version` and `docker info | grep Runtimes`
- nvidia runtime: `nvidia-container-cli info`
- k8s: `kubectl version --short` and `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
meera (eng-infra): I'll run those over ssh from bastion. Pasting commands I will run so we all have the outputs later: \n```
ssh ubuntu@10.20.5.12 -A \nssh ubuntu@10.20.5.18 'hostname && uname -r && lsb_release -a'\nssh ubuntu@10.20.5.18 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv,noheader'\nssh ubuntu@10.20.5.18 'sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 5'\nssh ubuntu@10.20.5.18 'nvcc --version || echo "nvcc missing"'\nssh ubuntu@10.20.5.18 'containerd --version || docker info | head -n 5'\nssh ubuntu@10.20.5.18 'nvidia-container-cli --version || echo "nvidia-container-cli missing"'\n```
ana (sales): thanks. Also Novus asked about kernel params: `vm.max_map_count` and `rmem_default` — are those required? They used Elastic in other infra.
sam (field-eng): For inference runtime we don't need vm.max_map_count specifically, but we do need large pinned memory pages sometimes for high-throughput. We'll note it as optional: set `vm.swappiness=10` and ensure `mlock()` capability for the runtime.
meera (eng-infra): quick note: on Ubuntu 22.04 + driver 535 we expect `nvidia` module present and `nvidia-smi` to succeed. If driver < 515, we might hit CUDA 12 incompatibilities. If `nvidia-container-toolkit` missing, containerd users should add the runtime config: `/etc/containerd/config.toml` snippet we use: \n```
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".containerd.runtimes.nvidia]
  runtime_type = "io.containerd.runc.v2"
  [plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".containerd.runtimes.nvidia.options]
    BinaryName = "/usr/bin/nvidia-container-runtime"
```
meera (eng-infra): Running now, will paste outputs. :eyes:
infra-bot: Ticket INF-2189 created for NovusHealth POC node validation (assigned to meera).
meera (eng-infra): Output snippet: `10.20.5.18, NVIDIA A10, 535.86.10, 24576 MiB` (nvidia-smi OK). `modinfo nvidia` shows version 535.86.10. `nvcc missing` — they only installed runtime / driver, no toolkit. containerd present (1.7.x). `nvidia-container-cli missing` — toolkit not installed.
sam (field-eng): Sounds fine. We'll need to install `nvidia-container-toolkit` on the node (apt packages) and restart containerd. Also install `cuda-toolkit` if they want local builds, but not required for serving.
nana (sales): Novus also wants to know how hosted API keys translate for Private. Short answer I gave: Hosted keys are not reused; for Private we generate a service principal and mTLS certs plus a short-lived token endpoint — will product doc capture that?
meera (eng-infra): Correct — Private RPC uses local service accounts + API tokens we issue for the customer's control plane. Need to confirm they have a KMS for key storage. I'll add a note to the ticket: confirm KMS/HSM or Redwood-managed keys.
sam (field-eng): For POC install prereqs we'll hand them this minimal checklist to run on all nodes: 
1) Ubuntu 20.04+ or RHEL 8+ and kernel >= 5.15
2) NVIDIA driver >= 525 recommended (535 tested)
3) Install nvidia-container-toolkit and restart containerd
4) Ensure containerd runtime config has `nvidia` runtime mapped
5) Kubernetes v1.25-1.27 supported for this build (we test on 1.26)
6) Open egress to package repos and Redwood control plane endpoints (list provided in ticket)
7) Confirm KMS and internal firewall rules for service account token exchange
meera (eng-infra): I pasted the node-level commands and partial outputs into INF-2189. Quick remediation steps I ran: \n```
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit\nsudo systemctl restart containerd
sudo systemctl status containerd --no-pager
containerd --version
```
meera (eng-infra): After restart, `nvidia-container-cli --version` returned `nvidia-container-cli 1.12.0` and containerd sees the runtime. `kubectl get nodes` from their control plane shows the node Ready.
nana (sales): perfect. Can we also confirm expected performance delta if they enable prefix caching and batching? Novus asked rough numbers to justify Dedicated vs Private.
sam (field-eng): give them a perf sheet: batching + KV prefix cache reduces token-cost by ~30-60% depending on prompt reuse; latency impact is configurable — we can run a small benchmark during POC once the node is in the cluster. I'll schedule that as follow-up in INF-2189.
nana (sales): thanks all. I'll reply to Novus with the checklist and estimated next steps. tagging :meera: :sam: for visibility. :thumbsup:
